questions.q: A number $N$ is formed by writing $999$ exactly $99$ times side by side. What is the remainder when $N$ is divided by $7$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling

Dekh bhai, seedhi si baat hai... ye cyclicity ka question hai jise dekh ke solve karna hai.

Pen-Free Observation: 7 ki divisibility mein 6 digits ka cycle chalta hai ($1001 \times 999 = 999999$). Yaani har 6 same digit block 7 se zero remainder deta hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Yahan 999, 99 times hai, toh total digits hue $99 \times 3 = 297$.
Ab 297 ko 6 se divide karega toh remainder aayega 3. Matlab shuru ki 294 digits 7 se poori divide ho jayengi.
Bachenge sirf aakhiri 3 digits yani $999$. Direct $999 \pmod 7$ nikal le, remainder $5$ aayega. Best method hai yeh time bachane ka!

Future Exam Takeaway: $10^6 \equiv 1 \pmod 7$, so digits repeating in blocks of 6 give remainder 0. Hamesha total digits nikal kar 6 se divide karo.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $(123456789101112\dots 444546)$ is divided by $16$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Tail Limit Observation)

Dekh bhai! Pura number dekh kar panic nahi hona hai, sirf base ki power pakad.

Pen-Free Observation: $16 = 2^4$, toh 16 ki divisibility check karne ke liye sirf number ki aakhiri 4 digits chahiye hote hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Yeh counting series chal rahi hai $44, 45, 46$ tak. Toh last 4 digits hue $4546$.
Ab bas $4546 \div 16$ kar. $16 \times 284 = 4544$ hota hai.
Remainder kya bacha? 2 bacha. Options eliminate kar aur aage badh!

Future Exam Takeaway: Divisibility of $2^n$ depends entirely on the last $n$ digits. Aage ke saare digits sirf daraane ke liye hote hain.

questions.q: What are the last two digits of $3^{2019}$?
questions.s: <b>Bhai isko 3⁴)⁵⁰⁴.3³ karke 81)⁵⁰⁴ .27 \= 8×4.27 \=567

Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Series Splitting)

Bhai, dhyan se dekh! Yeh do mixed telescoping series ka jhol hai. Ek flow mein add karne gaya toh fass jayega.

Pen-Free Observation: Isko 7 aur 11 wale numerators mein alag-alag split kar le.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Series 1: $7 \times (1/2 + 1/6 + 1/12 + \dots + 1/156) = 7 \times (1 - 1/13) = 84/13$.
Series 2: $11 \times (1/3 + 1/15 + \dots + 1/575)$. Yahan difference 2 ka hai denominators ke factors mein ($1\times3, 3\times5$), so formula lagega $\frac{1}{\text{diff}} \times (\text{first} - \text{last})$. $11 \times \frac{1}{2} \times (1 - 1/25) = 132/25$.
Dono ko jod de: $84/13 + 132/25 = 3816/325$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Mixed series are CGL mains traps designed to induce panic; separate them to reveal standard telescoping patterns.

questions.q: The non-terminating repeating decimal among the following fractions is:
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Base Properties)

Dekh bhai... fraction ko evaluate nahi karna, sirf denominator ke DNA ko padhna hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Fraction tabhi terminate hota hai jab uske denominator ke prime factors sirf 2, 5, ya dono hon ($2^n \times 5^m$).

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Option B dekh, $76 = 4 \times 19$.
Isme prime number 19 aa gaya, jo fraction ko non-terminating bana dega kyunki numerator 679 bhi 19 se completely divide nahi hota. Direct hack!

Future Exam Takeaway: Hunt for primes other than 2 and 5 in the denominator to instantly spot non-terminating fractions.

questions.q: Find the remainder when a 50-digit number formed by writing $123456789101112\dots$ is divided by $16$.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Digit Counting)

Dekh bhai... aise sawalon mein pura number nahi likhna hota, sirf aakhiri tak jump karna hai.

Pen-Free Observation: 16 se check karna hai, so only last 4 digits matter. Hume 50th digit locate karni hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Pehle 9 numbers mein 9 digits cover ho gaye. Bachi $50 - 9 = 41$ digits.
Ab sab 2-digit numbers hain ($10, 11, \dots$). 41 digits matlab 20 pure numbers aur ek single digit ($41/2 = 20$ remainder 1).
10 se shuru karke 20 numbers $29$ tak aayenge. Agla number 30 hona tha par ek hi digit leni hai, so sirf '3'.
String ends at $28293$. 16 se last 4 digits: $8293 \pmod{16} = 5$. Khatam!

Future Exam Takeaway: Jump to the end of the series using digit block counts (1-9, 10-99) instead of writing it out sequentially.

questions.q: Which of the following expressions is a factor of $(10^{12} - 1)$ but NOT a factor of $(10^6 - 1)$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Algebraic Factorization)

Dekh bhai, basic algebra zindabad! Badi values dekh ke darna nahi hai.

Pen-Free Observation: $10^{12} - 1$ ek $(a^2 - b^2)$ ka format hai jise tod ke answers milenge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
$(10^{12} - 1) = (10^6 - 1)(10^6 + 1)$.
Question mein condition hai ki $(10^6 - 1)$ ka factor nahi hona chahiye. Matlab humein $(10^6 + 1)$ ka factor dhoondhna hai.
$(10^6 + 1) = (10^2)^3 + 1$. Ise $(x^3+1)$ wale formula se kholega toh ek factor $(10^2 + 1) = 101$ aayega. Seedha nishana!

Future Exam Takeaway: $a^n \pm b^n$ basic identities break down the biggest numbers instantly. Difference of squares laga kar factors isolate karo.

questions.q: $xy$ is a number that is divided by $ab$ where $xy < ab$ and gives a result $0.xyxyxy\dots$ then $ab$ equals
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Fraction Conversion)

Dekh bhai... Isme toh pen uthane ki bhi zarurat nahi thi! Bar wale decimals ka logic seedha apply hota hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Two-digit repeating cycle $xyxyxy$ means the denominator must be based on 99.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
$0.xyxyxy\dots = 0.\overline{xy} = \frac{xy}{99}$.
Question ke mutabiq yeh value $\frac{xy}{ab}$ ke barabar hai.
Dono ko equate kar de: $\frac{xy}{ab} = \frac{xy}{99}$. Clear cut $ab = 99$ aa gaya.

Future Exam Takeaway: An $n$-digit repeating decimal pattern is always that number divided by $10^n - 1$ (e.g., 9, 99, 999). Direct observation gives the answer.

questions.q: In a farm, the ratio of the total number of heads to the total number of legs of pigs and ducks is 7:20. If there are 20 ducks in the farm, find the total number of pigs.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Cross-Product Method

Dekh bhai, jab fractions/ratios directly linked ho toh basic ratio method linear variables nikal deta hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Pig ke 4 pair, Duck ke 2 pair hote hain. Duck count fixed hai 20.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Maan le Pigs $P$ hain. Total heads = $P + 20$.
Total legs = $4P + 40$.
Question ne diya hai: $\frac{P + 20}{4P + 40} = \frac{7}{20}$.
Cross multiply karega toh $20P + 400 = 28P + 280$.
Solve kar, $8P = 120$, so $P = 15$. Approximation ya options rakh ke bhi check kar sakta tha. If 10 rakhte toh total head 30 banta jisme 7 hai hi nahi toh ratio kabhi 7 unit nahi aayega only 15 rakhne pe 35 banega jisme 7 hai.

Future Exam Takeaway: Simple linear ratios on 'Heads & Legs' problems equate directly. Don't overcomplicate with mixtures unless required.

questions.q: What is the sum of all the individual digits of the first 100 natural numbers (1 to 100)?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Symmetry Counting)

Dekh bhai... series add nahi karni, smart approach lagao. 0 to 99 ek perfect symmetric block hota hai.

Pen-Free Observation: 00 se 99 tak har digit (0-9) apne place par equally repeat karti hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
00 se 99 tak har digit exactly 20 baar aati hai (10 baar tens par, 10 baar units par, total 10 sets mein).
Sum of digits = $20 \times (0+1+2+\dots+9) = 20 \times 45 = 900$.
Bacha 100, iske digits ka sum hai 1.
Total ho gaya $900 + 1 = 901$. CGL level logic!

Future Exam Takeaway: Exploit symmetry in counting problems. The block 00-99 is your best friend for digit frequencies.

questions.q: If $732XY$ is a number which is divisible by 70, then find minimum value of $(X+Y)/2$.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Base Isolation)

Dekh bhai... composite rules ko humesha unit digit set karne ke liye pehle kaatna chahiye.

Pen-Free Observation: Number 70 se divisible hai toh 10 se bhi hoga, matlab aakhiri digit $Y$ strictly 0 ho gaya.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Ab bacha 7. $732X$ ko 7 se divide karna hai.
$7320 \pmod 7 = 5$. Toh $(5 + X)$ ko 7 se divisible banana hai.
Minimum $X$ aayega 2.
Value maangi hai $\frac{X+Y}{2}$ ki, toh $\frac{2+0}{2} = 1$. Option elimination aur digital hacks ka sahi prayog kar.

Future Exam Takeaway: Always satisfy the 10, 5, or 2 divisibility rule first to lock the unit digit, then solve for the remaining primes.

questions.q: If the 6-digit number $213x4y$ is divisible by 99, find the value of $(x + y)$.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Balancing)

Dekh bhai... 99 matlab 11 aur 9 dono se divisible hona chahiye. Aise case mein 11 ki condition hamesha linear equation deti hai.

Pen-Free Observation: 11 ka rule alternate digit sum hota hai, jo humein variables mein direct relation dega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
11 ka rule laga: Alternate sum $(2+3+4) - (1+x+y) = 9 - (1+x+y) = 8 - (x+y)$.
Yeh 11 se divisible tabhi hoga jab yeh 0 bane, kyunki $x, y$ digits hain aur inka max sum 18 ho sakta hai (so -3 possible nahi). So $x+y = 8$.
Cross check with 9: Sum of digits = $10+x+y = 18$, jo 9 se divisible hai. Done!

Future Exam Takeaway: For composite divisors like 99, 88, 72, always hit the 11 or 8 divisibility rule first. It locks the variables instantly.

questions.q: Find the total number of distinct prime factors of the product: $10! \times 11! \times 12! \times \dots \times 20!$
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling

Dekh bhai, seedha logic! Pura calculate karna hi nahi hai, numbers ka behavior samajh.

Pen-Free Observation: Factorials multiplication mein naye primes generate nahi hote, jo sabse bada boundary number hota hai, highest prime bas uske andar ka hota hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Yahan limit 20! hai, matlab jo prime numbers 20 tak hain, sirf wahi is pure product mein honge.
Primes $\le 20$ nikal: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19.
Count karega toh exact 8 aayenge. Aise questions ko second mein uda.

Future Exam Takeaway: Factorial products don't introduce new primes, they just increase the power of existing ones up to the highest boundary.

questions.q: What is the smallest number which when divided by 6, 8, and 10 leaves remainder 4, 6, and 8 respectively?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Deviation / Negative Remainder)

Dekh bhai... Jab har number pe alag remainder aaye toh unke gaps observe kiya kar, wahan hack chhupa hota hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Divisor aur Remainder ke beech ka difference check kar: $6-4=2$, $8-6=2$, $10-8=2$. Sabme common negative offset -2 aa raha hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Aise cases mein seedha LCM(6, 8, 10) nikal aur usme se constant difference minus kar de.
LCM hai 120.
Answer = $120 - 2 = 118$. Option se bhi har number ko divide karke direct remainder check kar sakta tha.

Future Exam Takeaway: Constant difference between divisor and remainder implies the answer format is $K \times \text{LCM} - \text{Difference}$. Block bana ke division method tab lagate hain jab successively divide kare mtlb jo quotient aaye usko divide karte jaaye but yahan koi number N hai usko hi sabse sivide karna hai.

questions.q: Find the number of factors of 14400 divisible by 18 but not by 36.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Combinatorics / Unitary Scaling

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... factors mein conditions set hain, iska matlab bas powers ko lock karna hai.

Pen-Free Observation: $18 = 2^1 \times 3^2$ and $36 = 2^2 \times 3^2$. Difference sirf power of 2 ka hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Prime factorize $14400 = 2^6 \times 3^2 \times 5^2$.
Divisible by $18$ matlab at least ($2^1 \times 3^2$) hona chahiye.
Not divisible by $36$ matlab ($2^2 \times 3^2$) nahi hona chahiye.
Requirement strict ho gayi: 2 ki power sirf $1$ ho sakti hai (1 choice). 3 ki power exactly $2$ rahegi kyunki max $3^2$ hi hai (1 choice). 5 ki power kuch bhi $0, 1, 2$ ho sakti hai (3 choices).
Combinations: $1 \times 1 \times 3 = 3$. Brilliant question!

Future Exam Takeaway: 'Divisible by X, not by Y' means lock the exact power of the prime that differs between X and Y.

questions.q: Find the maximum power of 3 in 60!
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Successive Change (Legendre's Formula)

Dekh bhai... Factorials mein prime powers nikalne ka universally fastest tareeqa lagana hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Divisors ko baar baar 3 se divide kar aur quotients ko add kar.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
60 ko 3 se divide kar: quotient 20.
Phir 20 ko 3 se kar: quotient 6.
Phir 6 ko 3 se kar: quotient 2.
Bas in quotients ko add kar de: $20 + 6 + 2 = 28$. Is hack se kabhi calculation error nahi aayega!

Future Exam Takeaway: Don't rely on complex summation notations; just successively divide the quotient by the prime and add the results.

questions.q: In a parking lot, there are only two-wheelers and four-wheelers. The total number of vehicles is 60 and the total number of wheels is 200. How many two-wheelers are parked there?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Shift Method)

Dekh bhai... Linear equations $x$ aur $y$ wali equations banayega toh time nikal jayega. Shift method se bina pen chalaye solve kar.

Pen-Free Observation: Maan le parking lot mein sabke paas 4 pahiye hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Toh total wheels $= 60 \times 4 = 240$ hone the. Lekin asal mein wheels sirf 200 hain.
Yeh 40 wheels jyada kyu aaye? Kyunki humne 2-wheelers ko bhi 4-wheeler ginn liya (matlab har 2-wheeler pe 2 extra pahiye assume kiye).
Extra wheels ko extra factor 2 se divide kar de: $40 / 2 = 20$. So, 20 two-wheelers the.

Future Exam Takeaway: Shift method avoids simultaneous equations completely. Shift all entities to the higher value and divide the error gap.

questions.q: Determine the last three digits of $9^{100}$.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Binomial Expansion)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Last 3 digits matlab calculation mod 1000 ki karni hai. Jab base 10 ke aas paas ho toh Binomial Theorem zindabad.

Pen-Free Observation: $9^{100} = (10 - 1)^{100}$. Expansion mein aakhiri 3 terms hi bachenge, baki sab 1000 se multiply hoke end mein $000$ denge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Expand karega toh aakhiri terms hongi: $\dots - \binom{100}{97} 10^3 + \binom{100}{98} 10^2 - \binom{100}{99} 10 + 1$.
Modulo 1000 karna hai, so higher powers cancel. Third last term $4950 \times 100 = 495000 \equiv 0 \pmod{1000}$.
Second last $-1000 \equiv 0$.
Aakhiri bacha sirf $+1$. So last 3 digits lock ho gaye $001$ par.

Future Exam Takeaway: For last 3 digits, shift the base to $\pm 1$ of a power of 10 and expand binomially. Most terms become zero instantly.

questions.q: If a number is divided by a divisor D leaves remainder 17. If the number 3N is divided by D leaves a remainder 5. Find the remainder when 4N is divided by D?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Remainder Balancing)

Dekh bhai... Remainder theorem mein equations banayi toh phasega. Seedha operation remainders pe karna hota hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Number 3 times hua toh remainder bhi $3 \times 17 = 51$ hona chahiye tha, par 5 aa raha hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Agar theoretical remainder 51 hai aur actual 5, matlab inka difference $(51 - 5) = 46$ divisor $D$ se cut gaya (multiple hai).
Since initial remainder 17 tha, toh rules ke according $D > 17$ hoga.
$46$ ke factors hain 23, 46. So $D$ is purely $23$ or $46$.
Ab $4N$ par aate hain, remainder should be $4 \times 17 = 68$.
Agar usko $D$ se divide kare (let's say 23), toh $68 = 23 \times 2 + 22$. Remainder hamesha 22 aayega. Mast concept!

Future Exam Takeaway: Theoretical remainder minus actual remainder is always a multiple of the divisor. Ek baar Divisor nikal gaya toh koi bhi multiple poch le.

questions.q: The simplification of $(1.\bar{3} \times 1.\bar{3} \times 1.\bar{3} - 1) / (1.\bar{3} \times 1.\bar{3} \times 1.\bar{3} + 1)$ is:
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling

Dekh bhai... Bar decimals ko algebraically handle karna sikho.

Pen-Free Observation: Expression is just $(x^3 - 1) / (x^3 + 1)$. Bar repeat logic laga kar fraction le lo.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
$1.\bar{3} = 1 + 3/9 = 4/3$. Direct substitution kar de.
Equation banegi $\frac{(4/3)^3 - 1}{(4/3)^3 + 1}$.
Ise khol: $\frac{64/27 - 1}{64/27 + 1} = \frac{37/27}{91/27}$.
Denominators (27) cancel hue, answer aa gaya $37/91$. Basic identity trap thi bas!

Future Exam Takeaway: Convert repeating decimals to fractions immediately before applying any algebraic identities to avoid calculation nightmares.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $(1^{49} + 2^{49} + 3^{49} + \dots + 49^{49})$ is divided by 50?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Symmetry Grouping)

Dekh bhai... Itni badi series add hone ke liye nahi bani hoti, ye sirf pairs mein cutne ke liye hoti hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Algebraic symmetric grouping. Formula yaad kar: $(a^n + b^n)$ hamesha $(a+b)$ se divide hota hai agar $n$ odd ho.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
First aur last term pakdo: $1^{49} + 49^{49}$. Sum of bases $1+49 = 50$. Toh yeh 50 se divisible hai.
Aise hi $2+48$, $3+47$ sab pairs zero remainder ban jayenge.
Beech mein sirf ek bichara bachega: $25^{49}$ kyunki iska pair nahi hai.
$25^n$ ko $50$ se divide karo toh remainder hamesha 25 aata hai (for any $n \ge 1$). Ans is 25.

Future Exam Takeaway: In massive series, look for first and last term symmetry to collapse the series into zero remainders.

questions.q: What is largest six digit number divisible by 52?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Approximation & Range Definition

Dekh bhai... Option se divide mat karne lag jana, standard bounded constraint approach best hai.

3-3 KE PAIR BNA LO AND DIFF FIND KARLOLAST WALA REMAINDER 15 DEGA AND FIRST WALA 39 AND BAKI TOH 4 SE DIV BHI NAHI HAI EK BAHUT CHHOTA HAI

Future Exam Takeaway: Direct division of the boundary number (like 999... or 100...) is faster than building multiples from scratch.

questions.q: What is the least common multiple (LCM) of $x^2-8x+15$ and $x^2-5x+6$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling

Dekh bhai... Polynomials ka LCM unke roots mein chupa hota hai. Isko normal numbers ki prime factorization ki tarah treat kar.

Pen-Free Observation: Dono quadratics ke basic factors dekhne hain jo visually clear hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Dono quadratics ko factorize kar.
Pehla: $x^2-8x+15 = (x-3)(x-5)$.
Doosra: $x^2-5x+6 = (x-2)(x-3)$.
LCM lene ke liye saare unique factors likh lo, jo common ho use ek baar likho.
Toh highest superset ban gaya $(x-2)(x-3)(x-5)$. Simple school level algebra.

Future Exam Takeaway: Treat polynomials like prime factorization of numbers. LCM combines all distinct roots to their highest power.

questions.q: If $N = 3^{14} + 3^{13} - 12$, What is the largest prime factor of N?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Algebraic Factorization)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Jab constants aur powers mix hon, toh factors isolate karke algebra laga.

Pen-Free Observation: 12 extract karke format ko square identities jaisa banaya ja sakta hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Common le pehle. $N = 3^{13}(3 + 1) - 12 = 4 \times 3^{13} - 12$.
12 common le le: $12(3^{12} - 1)$.
Ab $3^{12} - 1$ ko algebra se tod $(3^6 - 1)(3^6 + 1)$. $3^6$ hota hai 729.
Bracket ho gaye $728 \times 730$.
Factors break kar: $728 = 8 \times 7 \times 13$, aur $730 = 10 \times 73$.
Maximum bound prime factor perfectly 73 nikal gaya!

Future Exam Takeaway: Extract common constants to reveal standard $a^n - b^n$ algebraic identities. The largest prime is always hidden inside the factored brackets.

questions.q: If a 10-digit number $2094x843y2$, is divisible by 88, for the maximum possible value of x the value of (5x-7y) is?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Base Divisibility Balancing)

Dekh bhai... 88 jaisi badi values composite hoti hain. Inhe 8 aur 11 mein tod ke constraints satisfy karo.

Pen-Free Observation: Hamesha last 3 digits rule (8) pehle lagao taaki 'y' ki limited values mil jayein.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
88 matlab 8 aur 11.
Div by 8: last 3 digits $3y2$ chahiye. $y=1$ (312), $y=5$ (352), $y=9$ (392) satisfy karenge.
Ab 11 ka alternate sum: $(15+x+y) - 17 = x+y-2$. Yeh $0$ ya $11$ hona chahiye.
Max $x$ ke liye $x+y-2=11 \implies x+y=13$. Agar hum $y=5$ lenge toh $x=8$ perfectly set hota hai.
Equation mein dal: $5(8) - 7(5) = 40 - 35 = 5$. Question tod diya!

Future Exam Takeaway: Always find all possibilities for the unit digit from the $2^n$ rule before blindly applying the alternate sum 11's rule.
